column1: What is the main goal of variational inference?
column2: Variational inference approximates an intractable posterior distribution p(z|x) with a simpler distribution q(z), chosen from a tractable family of distributions.

column1: Why is variational inference needed in probabilistic models?
column2: Exact Bayesian inference is often impossible because computing the posterior requires evaluating an intractable integral or sum over latent variables.

column1: What is the variational objective function?
column2: The objective is to find the variational distribution q(z) that is closest to the true posterior p(z|x), usually by minimizing the KL divergence KL(q(z) || p(z|x)).

column1: What is the Evidence Lower Bound, or ELBO?
column2: The ELBO is a lower bound on the log evidence log p(x). Maximizing the ELBO is equivalent to minimizing the KL divergence between q(z) and the true posterior p(z|x).

column1: What is the standard ELBO formula?
column2: The ELBO can be written as ELBO(q) = E_q[log p(x,z)] - E_q[log q(z)], where the first term rewards explaining the data and the second term encourages entropy in q.

column1: How is the ELBO related to the posterior approximation?
column2: The log evidence decomposes as log p(x) = ELBO(q) + KL(q(z) || p(z|x)). Since the KL divergence is non-negative, maximizing the ELBO makes q(z) closer to the true posterior.
The mean-field assumption approximates the posterior by assuming that latent variables are independent under q, for example q(z) = product_i q_i(z_i).

column1: What is the benefit and drawback of the mean-field assumption?
column2: The benefit is that inference becomes easier and more scalable. The drawback is that dependencies between latent variables may be ignored, leading to an inaccurate posterior approximation.
Black-box variational inference is a general approach that estimates gradients of the ELBO using sampling, so the user does not need to derive model-specific update equations manually.

column1: How is variational inference used in probabilistic programming?
column2: Probabilistic programming systems allow users to define probabilistic models in code, and then apply automatic inference methods such as variational inference to approximate posterior distributions.
